reason: The dry soybean pods need gathering before they can be cooked, and the lined basket is suited to harvesting.
expectation: The basket will collect the soybean harvest.

effect: The soybean pods are gathered on a clean surface; they still need preparation and cooking.
reaction: The harvest connects the meal to the row that survived the storm.
reason: I’ll check how the gathered pods can be prepared for cooking; the next operation is not obvious.
expectation: The inspection should show what can be used to prepare or cook the beans.

effect: The pods are shelled into dry soybeans, ready for the next cooking preparation.
reaction: The cloth catching the beans is a practical detail.
reason: The beans need thorough cooking, and the solar cooking pot is the available cooker.
expectation: The beans will go into the pot for cooking, potentially with water.

effect: The beans must be combined with drinking water before the pot can be used.
reaction: The feedback makes the missing preparation step clear.
reason: The compatibility report identifies water as the next ingredient for the dry beans.
expectation: The beans will be prepared with water for cooking.

effect: The beans have been soaked, drained and rinsed, so they are ready for the cooking vessel.
reaction: The preparation sequence is clearer now.
reason: The soaked beans need thorough cooking, and the solar cooking pot is ready.
expectation: The beans will be cooked in the pot.

effect: The beans are thoroughly cooked, and the remaining goal is to add potatoes and serve the stew with lettuce.
reaction: Cooking the beans separately first makes the food-safety sequence clear.
reason: The potatoes need harvesting before they can join the cooked beans; the lined basket worked for the soybean harvest.
expectation: The basket will collect the potato harvest.

effect: The potatoes are harvested, washed and cut, ready to join the cooked beans.
reaction: The harvest makes the earlier planting feel consequential.
reason: The prepared potatoes can now join the thoroughly cooked beans in the pot.
expectation: The potatoes will be added to the beans and cooked into stew.

effect: The potatoes and beans are now cooked together as stew; fresh lettuce remains to be served.
reaction: The second heating completes the stew without overcomplicating the cooking sequence.
reason: The lined basket previously harvested lettuce from this same tray, so it should work again.
expectation: The basket will collect fresh lettuce leaves for the meal.

effect: The basket no longer has an available combination, so the earlier lettuce-harvesting method cannot be repeated here.
reaction: That was unexpected given the earlier harvest.
reason: I’ll check how the lettuce tray can now contribute to the meal.
expectation: The inspection will identify an available way to prepare or serve the lettuce.

effect: Inspecting the lettuce tray automatically served washed leaves with the stew and completed the chapter.
reaction: The supper is a satisfying payoff for the crops kept alive through the storm, though the direct tray-to-stew combination was unexpected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Harvesting the potatoes and making stew made the earlier planting and storm survival feel consequential. The separate bean-cooking step also explained a practical food-safety sequence.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the basket on the lettuce repeated a previously successful harvest method but produced no useful feedback beyond its having no available combinations.

surprise.text: The lettuce tray combined directly with the finished stew, automatically picking and washing the leaves; the basket used for the earlier lettuce harvest was not involved.

arbitrary.text: The unavailable basket and direct tray-to-stew combination felt somewhat arbitrary as gameplay, even though the final description made the physical preparation sensible.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the meal paid off the expedition’s growing work, and the practical preparation details made the progression engaging, despite the confusing lettuce interaction.
